title: acre works out the source edits that move a node by an offset
body:
`lang::parse` keeps a `Span` on every node, property and value, and `Object::source` is the span of the node that drew an object. Nothing maps a move of an object back to the numbers in the source that placed it.

## Proposal

A pure function in the library takes the source text, the parsed `Program` before expansion, a node span and an offset (dx, dy), and returns either a list of text edits (byte range and replacement) or a reason the node cannot move. It handles:

- `at X Y` with both values number literals in the node: add the offset.
- `at NAME DX DY` and `at ROW N DX DY`: add to the offsets, inserting ` DX DY` when they are absent.
- A node with no `at`, outside a stack or grid: insert `at X Y;` placing it where it is drawn.
- `points X Y ...` on a polygon or polyline: add to every pair.
- `from X Y` and `to X Y` literal ends on a line or arrow: add to each.

It refuses, with a reason a person can read: a value from a `let`, a `( ... )` expression or a `style`; a child of a stack or grid; a node inside a `repeat`; a node a timeline moves or scales; and an end that names a node. Numbers are written rounded to whole pixels unless the original had decimals.
